title: Chunk-affinity and tool/function-call compatibility sweep for pinned model snapshots and perf-profile publishing
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Background: New model onboarding flow creates pinned snapshots (model+tokenizer+quantization) and publishes a performance profile (latency/throughput/kv-behavior) that is used by routing and canary policies. We discovered intermittent failures when the runtime delivers output as chunked/partial stream frames while a tool/function call is being emitted by the model (function call JSON object split across stream boundaries). This ticket runs an explicit compatibility sweep to validate chunk boundary handling, function-call integrity, and perf-profile correctness for pinned model snapshots before they are published to the model catalog.
scope: Verify chunked stream semantics and tool/function-call reassembly across pinned model snapshots and quantization variants. Ensure perf-profile publishing job contains stream-aware metrics (per-chunk latency, function-call reconstruction error rate) and that pinned model rollouts will be blocked on a minimum compatibility bar.
out_of_scope: Runtime-level kernel selection changes or deep model architecture fixes; separate tickets will address kernel-tuning. This ticket focuses on verification, harnesses, and guardrails for publish pipelines.
deliverables: 1) Test harness for synthetic chunked output with injected chunk splits and toolcall fragmentation. 2) Perf-profile extension that records chunk-level metrics. 3) Canary checklist and gating rules for model catalog publish. 4) Docs for onboarding engineers describing incompatibility signatures and remediation steps.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned model snapshots pass the chunked-stream test harness for 3 representative sequence lengths (128, 1024, 4096) with function calls preserved 100% in normal and 99.5% in heavy-shared-batching scenarios.
Perf-profile publish job records chunk-level latency percentiles and a function-call-reconstruction metric; failure rate >0.5% flags the model as 'stream-fragile' and blocks automated publish.
Canary policy is updated to route 5% traffic to pinned snapshot only if the snapshot passes the compatibility sweep.
Playbook created with remediation steps: revert pin -> disable streaming -> adjust tokenizer/chunking -> republish perf profile.
test_plan: Create a deterministic harness that replays recorded model outputs but slices them at different byte/token offsets to simulate chunk boundaries. Add a fuzzing mode that randomly splits JSON function-call payloads across stream frames. Run the harness against the latest onboarding snapshot pipeline for each new model and quantized variant. Compare reconstructed function-call JSONs against ground truth and record metrics to the perf-profile job.
test_steps: 1) Checkout pinned snapshot artifact from artifact store (s3://redwood-onboard/snapshots/<model>-<pin>).
2) Launch local harness container that replays logits/decoding and emits chunked frames with configurable split patterns.
3) Inject simulated tool calls with nested JSON bodies and verify reassembly in runtime consumer (runtime-stream-consumer-test).
4) Run heavy-batching configuration to simulate shared GPU pipeline and measure reconstruction under 1000 concurrent small requests.
5) Publish perf-profile candidate and validate job outputs in perf-profile dashboard (grafana link).
6) If function-call reconstruction error > 0.5% for any tested config, tag snapshot as 'stream-fragile' and block publish pipeline.
progress_updates: 2026-03-01 Aisha Raman: Created ticket and initial test spec. Identified failing examples where function-call JSON was split across two frames and downstream tool integration raised parse errors.

2026-03-03 Diego Morales: Built prototype harness that replays recorded outputs and can emit deterministic splits. Early runs show 1.2% reconstruction failures for quantized-int8 variant on 1024 sequences under shared-batching.
2026-03-05 Diego Morales: Opened PR for harness and added CI job to run the harness against nightly onboarding snapshots (see PR list).

2026-03-08 QA (Jing Wei): Ran expanded fuzzing with 10k simulated tool-calls; identified two root causes: tokenizer edge-case causing off-by-one token split, and stream-framing buffer flush behavior in older runtime-stable nodes.
2026-03-10 Diego Morales: Added gating rule to perf-profile publisher and drafted canary rollout change. Pending security review for perf metrics ship (low sensitivity).
decisions: Adopt conservative default: block automated publish for any snapshot with function-call reconstruction rate > 0.5% across target sequence lengths.
Publish perf-profile metrics to internal perf pipeline only; do not expose chunk-level detailed traces in public catalog to avoid leaking model internals.
Create a remediation label 'stream-fragile' that surfaces on onboarding dashboards and halts auto-promotion until triaged.
Prefer harness-based verification in the pipeline rather than attempting to fix tokenizer heuristics in this ticket; tokenizer fixes will be a follow-up if needed.
test_results: Prototype harness run (2026-03-03) against three models: base(0.0% failures), quant-int8(1.2% failures at 1024), quant-4bit(0.6% failures at 4096). After tokenizer edge-case mitigation patch (PR 2831) quant-int8 dropped to 0.4% and quant-4bit to 0.35% in subsequent runs.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge harness PRs and enable CI check as optional for 1 cycle. 2) Enable gate in perf-profile publisher: fail on >0.5% reconstruction error. 3) Update onboarding console UI to show 'stream-fragile' flag. 4) Run manual canary: route 5% traffic to pinned snapshot for 48h, monitor function-call errors and latency. 5) If stable for 48h, promote to 25% then 100% per normal rollout.
notes: Related runtime issue: nodes with older libuv versions had earlier flush semantics that split frames more aggressively.
We should consider adding a small stream-header that indicates "remaining_bytes_for_object" but that requires model and tokenizer changes; track as RFC for Q2.
Customer support should be notified if we mark a widely-used model as 'stream-fragile' because it will delay their onboarding publish; CS contact: Priya Nair.
